claims.title: Snip internal URL shortener backend
claims.body: Build Snip, an internal URL shortener for the company used by marketing and the docs team. Must create short links, redirect fast, and later track click analytics.

claims.title: PostgreSQL is the source of truth
claims.body: Standardize on PostgreSQL as the primary datastore. Ops team knows Postgres well, it already runs in prod, and at expected volume (a few million links, low hundreds of QPS) a dedicated KV store is unwanted operational overhead. A Redis read cache may be added later if reads get hot, but Postgres remains source of truth. Settled — do not reopen.

claims.title: Random 7-char base62 short codes
claims.body: Short codes are random, 7 characters, base62 — exactly. Chosen over sequential ids to prevent enumeration. Format is externally committed: marketing printed it in a campaign and a partner contract references '7-character Snip codes'. This can never change; it is frozen.

claims.title: Unique constraint + retry on collision
claims.body: Handle random-code collisions with a unique constraint on the code column plus generate-check-retry on insert.

claims.title: 302 redirect via single indexed code lookup
claims.body: Redirect resolves via a single indexed lookup on the code column. Use HTTP 302 (not 301) to retain control and enable analytics interception later.

claims.title: Click tracking must not slow redirects
claims.body: Every redirect should record a click event (timestamp, referrer, coarse geo) without slowing the redirect. The write path must be fire-and-forget/async so redirects stay fast.

claims.title: DynamoDB/Redis as source of truth
claims.body: AI proposed DynamoDB or Redis as the primary datastore since key/value fits short-code→URL lookups and is fast.
claims.reason: Company is standardizing on PostgreSQL, which ops knows well and already runs in prod; at expected volume a dedicated KV store is unwanted operational overhead. Redis is allowed only as an optional later read cache, not source of truth.

claims.title: Auto-increment ids exposed in URLs
claims.body: AI proposed exposing the row's auto-increment id in the URL as the simplest short-code scheme.
claims.reason: Sequential ids are enumerable — anyone could walk /1, /2, /3 to scrape every link, and they leak how many links exist. Rejected in favor of random 7-char base62 codes.

claims.title: How to reserve/arbitrate vanity codes
claims.body: Custom vanity URLs (e.g. snip/blackfriday) collide with the random code space and users may fight over names. No decision yet on how to reserve or arbitrate vanity codes. Parked as an open question.

claims.title: Click analytics milestone
claims.body: Storage and redirect are done and deployed. Current milestone is click analytics: record a click event (timestamp, referrer, coarse geo) on every redirect without slowing it.

claims.title: Build async click-tracking write path
claims.body: Immediate next task: build the click-tracking write path as fire-and-forget so redirects stay fast.
